report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing (rule opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal, threshold 3, current ~25.01, activeAt 2026-11-25T23:05:43Z) and is backed by real frontend-proxy error spans: GET, POST and 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true / http.status_code=500 / otel.status_code=ERROR, and the 10-minute increase at 23:06:43 was ~1908 error spans. The egress operation name shows the proxy's upstream is frontend. The frontend Deployment was updated at 23:04:18 by manager "OpenAPI-Generator" (generation 2, Helm had applied at 22:56:57), which rolled a new ReplicaSet frontend-9fd6bd655 and deleted pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-wmtsx at 23:04:19, with the same image digest (config-only rollout). The new pod frontend-9fd6bd655-9zswv is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, but its pod spec sets dnsPolicy: Default (dnsConfig null) while all 25 other otel-demo deployments, including frontend-proxy, use ClusterFirst, and its logs show '14 UNAVAILABLE: Name resolution failed for target dns:cart:8080 / product-catalog:8080 / ad:8080 / checkout:8080 / recommendation:8080' from 23:05:09 onward. Cluster DNS itself looks intact (both coredns pods Running/Ready/0 restarts) and no NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo, so the evidence points to the frontend Deployment's dnsPolicy: Default pod template as the object behind the failing frontend pod and, through it, the frontend-proxy 5xx rate. Exact timing details remain partly unresolved (alert activeAt precedes the first non-zero sample of the sampled rule series, and the exact field diff of the 23:04:18 update is not recoverable).

Container frontend in pod frontend-9fd6bd655-9zswv logs repeated gRPC failures "Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: Name resolution failed for target dns:cart:8080", and the same message for product-catalog:8080, ad:8080, checkout:8080 and recommendation:8080, with timestamps 23:05:09.708–23:05:09.951 and again 23:06:44.987–23:06:46.801.

Before the alert, all otel-demo Deployments were scaled from 0 to 1 between 22:56:57 and 22:57:00 (a namespace-wide restart), and frontend-proxy spans recorded 500s with a frontend child span 'GET /api/recommendations' in error during 22:57:01–22:57:33, i.e. while the environment was starting up.

A cluster-wide DNS outage is not supported: both coredns pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo, and frontend-proxy (dnsPolicy ClusterFirst) still reaches the frontend pod, whose own logs show it receiving and failing requests, so the resolution failures are confined to the Default-dnsPolicy frontend pod.

A crash, OOM kill or restart loop on the frontend or frontend-proxy container is rejected: frontend-9fd6bd655-9zswv and frontend-proxy-77df9b8f7-c4v9d are Running and Ready with restart count 0, lastState empty and no crash evidence, even though the frontend application is failing.

HTTP status-code counters could not confirm the 5xx rate: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count exposes a 'service' label but queries filtered on service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy" and on service=~"frontend.*" returned no series at 23:06:43, so those metrics are unknown for these services.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
